defects.summary: The V1-3/V2-2 truncation fix replaced one false absolute with two more false statements, and the hazard it declares "not live" goes live with this very branch: the fleet bumper already slices a multi-block scoped per-source stream with head -20, and a headline can be orphaned from its command in a real PR body today.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:1961-1967 now says "What the cap DOES guarantee is the primary's own pair ... today's bumper slices only the primary-scoped, single-block run — so nothing is live. A scoped per-source slice would be a NEW consumer and would need its own guarantee; it does not inherit one here."

Both clauses are checkable and false. _agent-guidance IS on this machine (/home/user/_agent-guidance) and scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1538 slices `sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' <<< "$fed_check_out" | head -20` into the federated PR body. `fed_check_out` is built at :1021-1039 by CONCATENATING one `--check-current --only "$reg"` block per drifted source — literally "a scoped per-source slice", and it exists today, not in a future PR 2. Its own surrounding prose at :1524-1536 says so: "each block below was produced by `--check-current --only <that registry>`".

Worse, that branch is gated on FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE (bump-consumer-locks.sh:710-718), which is set true exactly when the generator's --help contains BOTH `--only` and `--repin-source` — the two flags this branch adds. So the slice the comment calls "not live" becomes live at the moment this branch merges, and the comment is false on day one rather than eventually.

MEASURED ORPHAN, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v3/fedslice.py. Each scoped federated block is 2 fixed lines (headline + `--repin --ref <sha> --repin-source '<reg>@'`) plus one line per difference. Two federated sources, srcA drifted by 17 skills, srcB by one:
  total lines: 22 | sliced: 20
  LAST KEPT : FAILED: file:///tmp/v3fed-.../srcB's bundles have moved on since fd3689b9...
  FIRST CUT :   python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref 4c89c385... --repin-sourc
  ORPHANED HEADLINE IN THE BUMPER'S FEDERATED PR BODY: True
The reviewer's PR body ends on a failure naming a registry with no command under it — the exact outcome the original absolute denied, now reachable through the bumper's live federated lane rather than only through the primary lane the fix reasoned about.

Secondary, same block: "What the cap DOES guarantee is the primary's own pair" is vacuous in precisely this lane — a scoped source-only run prints no primary block at all, so the one guarantee the comment offers does not apply to the slice that is actually live. The two new tests (test_the_bumper_cap_always_keeps_the_primary_headline_with_its_command / _can_cut_a_later_headline_from_its_command) both slice an UNSCOPED run, so neither covers the bumper's federated concatenation.

defects.summary: The V1-2 refusal and the V2-1 remediation line collide: on a lock that federates one registry twice, --check-current prints a --repin-source command that the same generator then refuses at exit 1, with no supported way to advance that pin — the same "the tool prints advice it does not accept" class the round just fixed as V1-7.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:853 raises for any --repin-source spec whose registry the lock federates twice; scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:2024-2025 prints `--repin [--ref <sha>] --repin-source '<registry>@'` for every drifted source without consulting that condition.

REPRODUCED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v3/deadend.py, on exactly the shape the round's own new fixture builds (_lock_federating_one_registry_twice, scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:3159):
  check-current exit 1
  FAILED: file:///tmp/v3dead-.../cms-platform's bundles have moved on since 12570a89... Advance that source's pin ... with:
    python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref a91673d2... --repin-source 'file:///tmp/v3dead-.../cms-platform@'
  RAN that line verbatim -> exit 1 | ERROR: --repin-source ...: this lock federates that registry twice, under [cms-platform; other] ... it will not pick one for you

Before cd1ad5f that command succeeded (over-broadly, advancing both — V1-2). After it, the drift is unrepairable by any documented route: the refusal's two escapes are "give that registry a single 'sources' entry" (change the lock's identity, not repair drift) and "restate the whole array with a plain generate" (which requires the operator to look up the new sha by hand and re-state every bundle/layout/ref). The refusal itself is right; printing a command the program will reject is what is new.

Not only a human path: _agent-guidance/scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1290 builds `repin_source_args+=(--repin-source "$reg@")` from the same per-registry list, so the nightly hits the same exit 1 on such a consumer lock. Nothing tests the intersection — test_repin_source_refuses_a_registry_the_lock_federates_twice never runs --check-current, and the new remediation tests only use singly-federated locks.

defects.summary: The new per-source identity probe added for V1-1 is described as proof of identity in a comment, a test docstring and its own error message, but it is defeated by a branch-name ref — the exact lock shape the SAME function's docstring (and a new test in this round) establishes as representable — so V1-1's exit-0 write of another repository's sha survives for that shape.
defects.evidence:
scripts/generate_skills_lock.py:885-886: "The pin the lock ALREADY carries is the proof: a checkout that is this registry has that commit." The probe is `_git(path, "cat-file", "-e", f"{source['ref']}^{{commit}}")` (:893), and `main^{commit}` resolves in ANY git repo with a main branch. Two paragraphs earlier, the same function's docstring (:800-806, added this round by 9232d18) says the opposite premise out loud: "`validate_ref` accepts a BRANCH name in a source's ref, so a lock can carry `\"ref\": \"main\"`" — and this round added test_an_unnamed_source_with_a_branch_ref_is_re_resolved and test_the_scoped_ok_line_names_the_resolved_ref_not_the_locks_raw_string, both of which hand-edit a source ref to `main`. So the branch takes that shape seriously everywhere except in the guard that claims the ref proves identity. scripts/test_generate_skills_lock.py:3225 repeats it ("The commit the lock already pins is the probe, exactly as it is for the primary"), and the runtime error at :896-901 asserts "this checkout is not that registry" on the same reasoning.

REPRODUCED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v3/branchprobe.py — the source's lock ref hand-written as `main`, the default ../cms-platform sibling replaced with a wholly DIFFERENT repo that also has a main branch, no --source-repo:
  lock source ref: main
  impostor HEAD: 35be95cf172c
  --repin --repin-source 'Adam-S-Daniel/cms-platform@' -> exit= 0
  Wrote ...: 2 skills from ..., Adam-S-Daniel/cms-platform@35be95cf172c98b25ebf24d45a9c8036b2dd1ef6.
  source ref now: 35be95cf172c | IS IMPOSTOR SHA: True
That is V1-1's headline outcome — another repository's commit written under the named registry at exit 0.

SCOPED HONESTLY: the CODE gap is symmetric and pre-existing, not new. Control /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/v3/ctrl.py: a lock generated with `--ref main`, its clone replaced by an impostor, bare `--repin` -> exit 0 writing the impostor sha; and that primary comment ("The pin already in the lock is the probe") is present at the branch point b81f6f1. What is new this round is the source-side comment, error text and test docstring restating it as an absolute inside a function that documents its own counterexample. Per the round's own rule ("do not fix code and leave the false prose standing"), the fix that closed V1-1 for 40-hex refs left prose asserting more than the guard delivers; either the sentences get the same `for a ref that is already a 40-hex sha` qualification 9232d18 applied to the byte-identical claim, or both probes reject a non-sha pin.

Re-ran the verifier's own harness scratchpad/atk/a2_default_sibling.py verbatim: [bare --repin] exit=1 (pre-existing guard), [--repin-source] exit=1, lock unchanged, decoy sha absent. Previously exit=0 writing the fork's HEAD. Negative control: neutering the new probe to `if False:` makes test_repin_source_refuses_a_checkout_that_is_not_the_source_it_names go red, so the gate is wired to something. Residue for a branch-name ref is reported as a separate defect.

V1-2 BLOCKING (one --repin-source spec fanning out across two entries sharing a registry) — CLOSED. Re-ran scratchpad/atk/b_dupreg.py: exit=1 with "this lock federates that registry twice, under [cms-platform; other]", both pins byte-unchanged (b38db14a / 95981086 held). Previously exit=0 with both moved to one new sha. Negative control: neutering `if len(known[reg]) > 1:` to `if False:` turns test_repin_source_refuses_a_registry_the_lock_federates_twice red. Module docstring and _apply_repin_sources docstring both now state refusal rather than the old "advances ONE of them".

V2-1 SHOULD-FIX (federated remediation omitted --ref and advanced the primary as a side effect) — CLOSED, verified end to end rather than by reading the string. Harness scratchpad/v3/anchor.py builds a primary deliberately ahead of its pin plus a drifted source, PARSES the printed line with shlex and RUNS it: printed `--repin --ref fb79a1c4... --repin-source 'file://.../cms-platform@'`; repin exit 0; PRIMARY HELD: True (fb79a1c4 -> fb79a1c4, generated_from unchanged); SOURCE ADVANCED: True. The verifier's own probe.py still shows the old symptom only because it hardcodes the un-anchored invocation instead of following the printed one. The anchor is correctly dropped when the primary drifted too (scratchpad/atk/e_truncation.py shows the bare form in that case).

V1-4 / V2-3 SHOULD-FIX (--only '' bypassing both argparse guards) — CLOSED. Re-ran scratchpad/atk/c_only_empty.py and scratchpad/bc2/probe.py P4: plain generate with --only '' now exit 2, lock byte-unchanged, `sources` still present, DE-FEDERATED: False (was exit 0 with the lock rewritten and registry reset to DEFAULT_REGISTRY); --check --only '' now exit 2 (was exit 0 printing an unscoped OK). Guards read `args.only is not None` at :1742 and :1744 and the sibling --repin-source guard at :1725 matches. `--check-current --only ''` still exits 1 via validate_registry, which is correct.

V1-3 / V2-2 SHOULD-FIX (the falsified truncation absolute) — the SENTENCE is closed: grep for "can never separate a headline" now hits only the two places that quote it in order to call it false (generate_skills_lock.py:1949 inside "That is false", and test_generate_skills_lock.py:913 in the counterexample test's docstring), and the docstring of test_every_failed_line_is_followed_by_its_own_remediation_command no longer repeats it. The replacement prose is a fresh defect and is reported above.

V1-5 NIT ("comes back by reference, so it serializes byte-identically") — CLOSED as prose. Re-ran scratchpad/atk/d_branchref.py: the unnamed source still moves (UNNAMED SOURCE MOVED TO THE NEW COMMIT: True), which is the pre-existing behaviour the fix deliberately kept; the docstring at :790-806 now separates by-reference from byte-identical, qualifies the latter to 40-hex refs, and names test_an_unnamed_source_with_a_branch_ref_is_re_resolved as the measurement. Re-ran scratchpad/atk/f_layoutclaim.py: the message now reads "That is two entries with two bundle lists, each with its own layout and ref"; "different layouts" is gone while the source's layout is measurably identical to the primary's (both plugins/{bundle}/skills). Verified myself: `git diff --stat ag58-pre-swap 0faa49d` is empty (identical tree at the pre-swap tip), the tag ag58-pre-swap still resolves to 2ebef216; at 06a03a9 the generator has --repin-source (12 occurrences) and does NOT print the federated headline (grep for "bundles have moved on since" -> no match), and 7988e59 is where that line appears. V2-5 NIT (cross-repo debt discharged without recording the reverse pointer) — CLOSED as far as this repo reaches, and the counterpart is real: /home/user/_agent-guidance/scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1254 still carries "A SIBLING SITE MOVES WITH THIS, and it is not editable from here." The new comment at generate_skills_lock.py:1274-1285 names that file, that heading, and the quoted paragraph, and test_the_cross_repo_anchor_comment_names_its_counterpart_block asserts all three plus that the quoted paragraph survives only as the quotation. The test unwraps comment prose before matching, so a reflow cannot silently break the link, and it reads only this repo's own file — deterministic.

V2-4 NIT (rejected: no skills-shrink guard on --repin-source) — the REJECTION's premise verified independently. Re-ran the fix author's scratchpad/probe_shrink.py: (A) bare --repin on a shrinking PRIMARY -> exit 0, ['adam/alpha','adam/beta'] -> ['adam/alpha']; (B) --repin --repin-source on a shrinking SOURCE -> exit 0, ['adam/alpha','cms-platform/deploy','cms-platform/publish'] -> ['adam/alpha','cms-platform/deploy']. Identical behaviour and identical exit code, so the gap does not distinguish the new flag and the deferral to _agent-guidance's skills_shrink_reason is a defensible scoping call. Recorded in stillOpen rather than dropped. The related pre-existing tarfile.ReadError traceback on an emptied source tree also still reproduces (scratchpad/bc2/probe.py P2) and is likewise recorded.
